oracle.explanation: The oracle loads the installed `next` package's compiled `NextNodeServer` class (`next/dist/server/next-server.js`), the same class instantiated by `next()`/custom servers, and drives its real `handleRequest` method in-process (no sockets or child processes) against a fabricated single-middleware manifest guarding `/protected`. It overrides `getMiddleware`/`runMiddleware` only to record invocation (not to implement the security check itself), so the actual decision of whether to call `runMiddleware` at all for a given request is made entirely by the installed package's own `handleRequest` logic, which on vulnerable 15.2.2 trusts the client-controlled `x-middleware-subrequest` header to mean 'this is an internal re-entrant subrequest, skip middleware', and on patched versions ignores/strips that header for externally-originated requests. First, a benign request without any forged header is dispatched and must result in middleware executing (setting a marker header) for operation_completed to become true. Only then is a malicious request sent with `x-middleware-subrequest: middleware` forged to match the middleware's own manifest name; if middleware is skipped (not invoked) this reproduces CVE-2025-29927's authorization bypass and exploit_succeeded is set true, whereas if middleware still runs (or the call throws, treated as blocked) exploit_succeeded is false. Any setup, module-resolution, or benign-call failure is caught and reported with operation_completed=false, never conflating a crash with a blocked exploit.
